value: el-classical-v1 enters by the architecture's standing bet: tables into a pack, no code into the engine. Greek withdraws two English conveniences — the word as atom of meaning, position as bearer of role — and replaces them with data: a stem-fold paradigm (the admission gate's diacritic fold, one level down) and a case-to-role map (the deed-finder's positional convention, replaced). Two laws gain Greek-specific force and are RECed below: the verb ending is a bound pronoun (a constraint bundle resolved by the existing signal substrate), and agreement is binding by morphological matching, never adjacency. One fate is added to the accounting taxonomy: grammar — an ending is not a stopword and not droppable; it is the role mark. Seqs in this fragment renumber on append.

affinity: Classical and Koine Greek prose: Attic historians and philosophers, the orators, the Septuagint and New Testament narrative. Fully inflected; pro-drop (subject lives in the verb ending); free word order with case-marked roles; postpositive particles; polytonic orthography; speech attributed by ἔφη/εἶπε with mid-quote parentheticals.

value: SUB-WORD SPLIT. A Greek word is stem + grammar. The tokenizer's unit of indexing is per-register data: tokens in this register split at the paradigm boundary. The stem routes to the index as a term and serves as the site key; the ending routes to the new fate 'grammar' — never dropped, never stopworded, never counted against the every-word law. The forms map every site already carries holds the attested inflected surfaces, exactly as it holds case-clothes today (Κῦρος, Κύρου, Κύρῳ, Κῦρον are one site keyed on Κυρ- with four entries in forms).

BOUND PRONOUN. A finite verb ending is a constraint bundle {person, number, voice} with no committed referent — structurally identical to a freestanding pronoun, delivered as a suffix. With pro-drop the subject often exists only there. On reading a finite verb with no overt nominative in its clause: mint/touch a subject signal carrying the ending's constraints and resolve it against active sites by the standard mass/momentum/δ-dominance activation law. When two candidates pull comparably, stall as NUL with reason 'competing' — the same honesty every reader owes. The engine does not care that the constraints arrived as a suffix.

AGREEMENT IS MATCHING, NOT ADJACENCY. Modifier-head and article-noun binding resolves by the anaphora comparator: which active span satisfies these case/number/gender constraints — at any distance within the clause. σοφός finds its noun from across the sentence. ὁ δέ at clause start is switch-reference: article + postpositive δέ mints an anaphor signal constrained to the most recent NON-subject candidate of matching gender/number. Genuine agreement ambiguity stalls with 'competing'; the comparator never breaks ties by proximity alone.

CASE IS THE HINT, NOT THE ORDER. The deed-finder for this register reads the finite verb wherever it sits and assigns CON endpoints from morphology, per el-classical-v1:case_roles. The emitted CON does not remember how its endpoints were found; the checker stays order-blind; BINDING law unchanged. Only the finding convention differs from en.

ASPECT AND GRAIN. The aorist/imperfect contrast (ἔλυσε once vs ἔλυε habitually) is not about finding the deed but about its temporal grain on the Time axis. Provisional convention: secondary endings on the present stem (imperfect) mark the bond Pattern-grain; aorist stem marks Figure-grain. This anticipates bonds carrying their grain and the Stance face ceasing to be op-fixed — the cube note in the appendix. Held as revisable assertion; vetoes append here.

The article is a free agreement probe: every occurrence broadcasts {case, number, gender} onto the span it heads. It is the cheapest evidence the matcher gets and the anchor of the ὁ δέ switch-reference pattern. Never index it as a term; its fate is grammar.

value.note: stem-final consonant interacts with σ (γ/κ/χ+σ→ξ, β/π/φ+σ→ψ, dental drops); fold table applies before stem extraction

value: STEM FOLD. Site admission folds the closed paradigm of endings off the stem before the two-sighting gate runs. The site key is the stem; the inflected surface lands in forms. This is the diacritic fold (Guzmán ≡ guzman) one level down, and the zh sub-word gram-mining under the same two-sighting law. Fold order: crasis-expand, elision-restore, movable-ν strip, augment strip (verbs), ending strip per declension/conjugation class. Ambiguous strips (a surface parsing under two classes) admit both candidate stems provisionally; the two-sighting law settles which is real. The mechanism is universal and inert when these tables are empty, exactly like the chrome gate.

value.syllabic: ἐ- prefixed to consonant-initial stems in secondary tenses; strip before stem match (ἔλυε → λυ-)
value.temporal: initial vowel lengthens (α/ε→η, ο→ω); fold lengthened vowel back as a stem-variant candidate
value.scope: indicative secondary tenses only; the augment is itself evidence of secondary tense and feeds grain_hint

value.nom: source_ref of the clause's CON; also the referent the bound-pronoun signal commits to when overt
value.acc: target_ref of the clause's CON; double-accusative emits two CON edges sharing source_ref
value.dat: additional CON edge with case folded into the relation (gave>to>); also instrument/means when no recipient reading survives
value.gen: additional CON edge folded as of>/from>; possession is a DEF on the possessor's site when stable, a CON when evental
value.voc: no CON; touches the addressee's site (address is contact, not predication)

value: GENITIVE ABSOLUTE: a genitive noun + genitive participle pair outside the main clause's argument structure is its own predication — emit its own CON with the genitive noun as source_ref. Greek sentences routinely carry several; each is just an extra bond per sentence.

MIDDLE VOICE GUARD. Middle morphology with the subject acting on itself or in its own interest does not create a reflexive CON: the existing guard keeping sRef ≡ oRef out of CON already covers half; the other half is convention — true middles (deponents: ἔρχομαι, βούλομαι, γίγνομαι) read as plain active deeds, and the middle-as-self-benefit nuance lands as a DEF shading on the bond, never a second endpoint.

ἔφη/εἶπεν induce from the quote slot exactly as 'says' did for ev-0 and 道 for zh; speech still needs agency. The mid-quote parenthetical φησί / ἦ δ' ὅς is the raya-insert pattern es already handles: the attribution interrupts the quoted span without closing it. ὅτι + finite verb after a speech verb opens indirect discourse — emit the speech CON without a quoted-span anchor.

Postpositives never open a clause — second position is their signature, which makes them free clause-boundary evidence: the token BEFORE a postpositive is clause-initial. μέν...δέ pairs mark contrastive structure (a SYN edge between the two clauses' bonds, weight low). Their fate is grammar: discourse glue, never indexed terms.

value.surface: clause-initial article (ὁ/ἡ/οἱ/αἱ) + δέ with no following noun in agreement
value.reading: anaphor constrained to most recent non-subject candidate matching gender/number
value.resolution: standard comparator with standard stall rights; 'the other one' is a constraint, not a guess

value: Freestanding pronouns decline like nouns: each member here is a stem whose paradigm lives in forms via the stem fold, and each occurrence carries {person, number, gender, case} constraints into the same comparator the bound endings use. αὐτός oblique = plain anaphor (him/her/it); αὐτός nominative or in attributive position = intensive/identity, a DEF shading, not a new referent. An overt nominative pronoun alongside a finite verb is EMPHASIS — the bound pronoun already supplied the subject; the overt form adds contrast weight, not a second signal.

Prepositions are stopwords for indexing but evidence for case_roles: ὑπό + genitive after a passive verb marks the agent — fold as by> on the passive clause's CON, restoring the demoted source_ref. The negatives οὐ(κ/χ)/μή flip the clause's bond polarity (a DEF on the bond), never delete it: an asserted absence is still an assertion.
final ν on 3sg/3pl verb forms and dative plurals (-σι(ν), -ε(ν), φησί(ν)) is euphonic: fold ν-present ≡ ν-absent for all matching

Crasis and elision expand BEFORE the sub-word split, so κἀγώ yields two tokens (καί + ἐγώ) each meeting its own fate. Pure fold rules in the pack; the engine's fold mechanism is the one the diacritic gate already owns.

value.iota_subscript: ᾳ/ῃ/ῳ ≡ ᾱι/ηι/ωι (adscript editions fold to subscript)
value.accent_fold: acute ≡ grave (the grave is positional); circumflex distinct; breathing marks NEVER folded — rough vs smooth distinguishes stems (ὅρος boundary vs ὄρος mountain after accent, εἷς one vs εἰς into)
value.accent_caution: full accent-strip only at the admission gate's last resort, because τίς/τις (who?/someone) and ἤ/ἦ (or/truly) are accent-minimal pairs; record any accent-folded admission with basis 'accent-fold' so it is auditable

value: NAMES UNDER INFLECTION. Proper names enter by the same two-sighting gate as everywhere — but sightings count at the STEM after the fold. Κῦρος in the nominative and Κύρου in the genitive are two sightings of one candidate site keyed Κυρ-, and the gate that already knows Guzmán ≡ guzman needs no new law to know it. The forms map holds the attested case-clothes; capitalization is editorial in this register (manuscripts had none), so the Latin-script case heuristic for name admission is OFF and the zh gram-mining path is the fallback shape.

Nothing above touches engine physics. The gate, signals, activation, stalls, settlement, and frames remain constraint-shaped. This module is a few hundred rows of paradigm data that have not changed in two millennia — the most stable convention a ledger will ever admit. Every entry is an assertion, linked and revisable; vetoes append; the graph hydrates.
